issues.legal_issue: The party alleging that a disputed document is forged bears the initial burden of proving that allegation unless the required fiduciary relationship and active confidence are established.
material_facts: The plaintiff brought a declaratory suit alleging that the sale deed was forged and fabricated, while the defendant denied the allegation and maintained that the deed was valid and genuine.
The defendant possessed the original sale deed.
The defendant denied the plaintiff’s allegations of a fiduciary relationship and active confidence between the parties.

The trial court reframed the issue to ask whether the deed was valid and genuine, placing the burden on the defendant; the High Court upheld that order based in part on the defendant’s possession of the deed and the plaintiff’s difficulty in proving a negative.
issues.conclusion: The initial burden was on the plaintiff, who asserted forgery. The defendant’s possession of the deed and the difficulty of proving a negative did not alter that burden. The order reframing the issue was set aside and the original issue was restored, while the trial court remained free to frame any additional issue it considered necessary.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 101 and 102 of the Evidence Act, the party asserting the affirmative bears the initial burden, which does not shift merely because the opposing party possesses the relevant document or because proof may be difficult. Pleadings are not evidence. The burden of proof remains fixed, while the onus of proof may shift as evidence is assessed; once the plaintiff discharges the initial onus and makes out a case for relief, the defendant may have to prove circumstances that would disentitle the plaintiff to relief. The Court relied on R.V.E. Venkatachala Gounder v. Arulmigu Viswesaraswami & V.P. Temple and Anr. and distinguished Krishna Mohan Kul @ Nani Charan Kul & Anr. v. Pratima Maity & Ors., where the relevant evidence had been adduced.

predicates.document_challenged_as_forged: A party brings a suit seeking relief on the basis that a document is forged or fabricated.
predicates.plaintiff_asserts_forgery: The plaintiff asserts that the disputed document is forged or fabricated.
predicates.fiduciary_confidence_not_established: The plaintiff has not established that the opposing party stood in a fiduciary relationship or position of active confidence.

issues.definition: When a plaintiff challenges a document as forged and has not established fiduciary confidence, the plaintiff bears the initial burden of proof.

issues.legal_issue: The burden of proving a transaction’s good faith shifts to the party in a position of active confidence only after that relationship and position have been established, and only when the transaction’s good faith is in question.
material_facts: The plaintiff alleged forgery and the defendant denied both the allegation and the asserted fiduciary relationship.
The courts below proceeded on the basis that the defendant was in a dominant position, but the defendant had not admitted or acknowledged the alleged relationship.
The dispute had not reached the stage at which evidence established a fiduciary relationship or active confidence.
issues.conclusion: The burden could not be placed on the defendant to prove the transaction’s good faith without first establishing the alleged fiduciary relationship and active confidence. Section 111 applies to a question about a transaction’s good faith, not to a question about its real nature.
issues.legal_principle: Section 111 of the Evidence Act places the burden of proving good faith on the party in a position of active confidence when the good faith of a transaction between the parties is in question. The relationship and active confidence must first be established before the presumption and resulting burden apply. The Court explained the principle discussed in Krishna Mohan Kul @ Nani Charan Kul & Anr. v. Pratima Maity & Ors. and distinguished it because the relevant relationship and evidence in that case had been established.

predicates.good_faith_of_transaction_disputed: A party challenges whether a transaction between the parties was conducted in good faith.
predicates.active_confidence_established: The evidence establishes that one party stood in a relationship of active confidence toward the other.

issues.definition: When a transaction’s good faith is disputed and active confidence is established, the party in that position must prove the transaction’s good faith.
